title: Accept the worktree root as a gate input root
description:
Gate input declarations accept `.` as a root covering the whole worktree, and the files jit itself writes during a mutation never enter an input digest, so recording gate results can never invalidate a reusable verdict.

## Background

A gate verdict is reused when its verdict declaration and the bytes under its declared input roots are unchanged (`crates/jit/src/domain/repository_inputs.rs`; the walker in `crates/jit/src/gate_execution.rs:387-497`). Two gaps make that reuse fragile.

`.` is rejected as a root: `DeclaredRoot::try_from` (`repository_inputs.rs:80-92`) applies the safe-relative-path predicate that profile package paths share (`:451-477`), so acceptance belongs in `DeclaredRoot` and in its `covers` method (`:59-63`), not in the shared predicate. The walker already handles an empty prefix (`gate_execution.rs:483`). Without `.`, a repository keeps a hand-written list of top-level roots, and a new top-level file silently escapes the digest.

The walker skips only `.git`. A data root nested in the worktree is digested whenever a root covers it, so each tracker write changes the digest unless the repository excludes record paths by hand. Excluding the whole data root is unsound: it also holds configuration that checkers read (gate, rule, invariant and template registries, schemas, reference pages), and a configuration edit would then reuse a stale verdict. The sound exclusion is the set of paths jit writes during a mutation: issue records, the event log, gate-run records, the index, locks, the record scratch directory, worktree state, and the worktree-root bootstrap lock. The storage layout constants already name them (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/path.rs`, e.g. `RECORD_SCRATCH_DIR` and `BOOTSTRAP_LOCK_FILE`) and follow a relocated data root. The nested-data offset (`path.rs:443,468-473`) is private and needs a crate-visible accessor. The walker receives the excluded prefixes as data, so the domain stays pure.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: An input declaration with root `.` is accepted, and its digest covers each worktree file that neither the declaration nor the mechanism excludes.
- [hard] REQ-02: Writing an issue record, an event, a gate-run record, the index, a lock, the record scratch directory, or worktree state leaves each gate's input digest unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: Editing a configuration file under the data root changes the digest of a gate whose roots cover it.
- [hard] REQ-04: The excluded set derives from the storage layout's path constants and follows a relocated data root; the walker hard-codes no data-root spelling.
- [hard] REQ-05: The custom-gates how-to states that `.` is a valid root and that tracker-written paths never enter a digest.
- [hard] REQ-06: Unit tests over the declared-root type and the digest walker own these properties.

## Notes

With these properties, gating several issues over unchanged checker inputs executes each checker once, whatever the tracker commits between evaluations. Removing the commit-based skip and the dirty-tree field is separate work that edits other functions of the same execution module.

planning.outcome: A `.` input root covers the worktree, and paths jit writes during a mutation never enter an input digest.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One root-acceptance rule plus one layout-derived exclusion set feeding the existing walker.

title: Declare this repository's tree-wide gate inputs as the worktree root
description:
This repository's tree-wide gates declare the worktree root as their one input root, excluding only generated or ignored trees, and the `secret-detection` gate stops reusing verdicts.

## Background

Five gates in this repository's gate registry (`.jit/gates.toml`) hand-keep the same 26-root list, about 130 root lines, plus about 60 exclude lines that remove tracker records from the digest: `cargo-ci` (`:54-96`), `cargo-ci-features` (`:122-164`), `docs-mechanical` (`:311-353`), `secret-detection` (`:568-606`) and `tests` (`:657-699`). The list already misses tracked inputs: `.config/nextest.toml` is read by the Rust CI script (`scripts/cargo-ci.sh:134-136`) but sits under no declared root, and the tracked empty `.index.lock` is uncovered. The git-ignored `.agents/cache-pool` (about 9.9 GB) lies under the `.agents` root and is walked on each tree-wide evaluation.

The engine now accepts `.` as a root and excludes the paths it writes during a mutation from each digest, so each list can collapse to the worktree root plus excludes for generated trees.

`secret-detection` digests issue records on purpose: a secret pasted into an issue record must be scanned. Once tracker-written paths leave the digest, reusing its verdict would pass a record that gained a secret, so that gate declares no inputs and executes on each evaluation.

This is repository-local configuration; it changes no shipped default.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `cargo-ci`, `cargo-ci-features`, `docs-mechanical` and `tests` each declare `.` as their only root, with excludes naming only generated or git-ignored trees such as `target/` and `.agents/cache-pool`.
- [hard] REQ-02: `secret-detection` declares no inputs and executes on each evaluation.
- [hard] REQ-03: No exclude in the gate registry names a tracker-written record path.
- [hard] REQ-04: Evaluating one of the four tree-wide gates twice over unchanged inputs, with a tracker commit between the evaluations, reuses the first verdict.
- [hard] REQ-05: A change to `.config/nextest.toml` changes the input digest of `cargo-ci`.
- [hard] REQ-06: Repository validation passes over the edited registry.

planning.outcome: This repository's tree-wide gates digest the worktree root minus generated trees, and secret scanning runs on each evaluation.

terminal.test_boundary: gate digest reuse across a tracker commit
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One registry file whose five root lists collapse to one declaration each.

title: Record built-in checker faults as error runs
description:
A built-in gate checker that cannot judge the repository records an `error` run instead of a `failed` verdict or no run at all, so each gate-run record distinguishes a checker fault from a verdict on the content.

## Background

Gate runs already carry an `error` status for exec checkers that time out, cannot be started, or are killed (`GateRunStatus`, `crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs:1098-1112`; mapping `crates/jit/src/gate_execution.rs:148-155`). An errored run is never reused (`types.rs:1022-1027`), so the next evaluation retries it.

Built-in checker kinds (`crates/jit/src/declarations/gates.rs:108-147`, dispatch `crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs:1052-1242`) record only passed or failed, synthesizing exit 0 or 4 (`gate_check.rs:1170-1174,1217-1221`):

- Repository validation folds a structural or integrity fault into a blocking finding recorded as failed (`gate_check.rs:646-672`).
- Label-target validation turns a misconfigured namespace or count into a blocking finding (`gate_check.rs:1108-1132`).
- Rule validation turns a missing or misconfigured rule into an error-severity finding recorded as failed (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:1413-1430`).
- Issue validation, and configuration or declaration load failures in each kind, propagate as errors with no run recorded (`gate_check.rs:468-469,476-477,535-536,558-559`; `validate.rs:1405-1411`). The process then exits with the gate error code, or 1 without JSON output, never the runner-error code (`ExitCode::ExternalError`, 10).

Evaluation already reports a recorded `error` run from an exec checker with the runner-error code and JSON verdict `error`, so a built-in checker that records such a run reaches the same reporting.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A built-in checker that cannot load its configuration or declarations records a run with status `error`.
- [hard] REQ-02: A repository-integrity or configuration fault met by a built-in checker records `error`, while a finding about repository content records `failed`.
- [hard] REQ-03: An evaluation that records an `error` run from a built-in checker exits with the runner-error exit code and reports verdict `error` in JSON output.
- [hard] REQ-04: The existing `error` run status carries the fault; no run status is added.
- [hard] REQ-05: Harness tests over gate checking own the classification for each built-in checker kind.

planning.outcome: A built-in checker that cannot judge records an error run, and evaluation exits with the runner-error code.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One classification rule applied at the built-in checker dispatch, reusing the existing error-run reporting.

title: Archive derived documents with their issue
description:
Archiving an issue moves the files under its artifact directories with it, so a document an issue owns by location is archived the same way as an explicitly linked one.

## Background

An issue's derived documents are the files under its resolved artifact directory in each declared documentation area; they belong to the issue without an explicit link. Archive planning takes its roots from explicit links only (`crates/jit/src/domain/artifact_inventory.rs:284-290`; `crates/jit/src/domain/artifact_discovery.rs:314-330,501-520`), and archive execution rewrites the linked document paths (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/archive.rs:175-190`). A derived document is therefore left behind in the active area when its issue is archived. Whether the archive classifier otherwise sweeps unlinked files under a short-id directory is unverified.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Archiving an issue moves each of its derived documents to the archive location, beside its linked documents.
- [hard] REQ-02: Archive planning lists derived documents among the issue's archive roots, so a preview shows them.
- [hard] REQ-03: A derived document that is also explicitly linked moves once.
- [hard] REQ-04: An issue with no derived documents archives exactly as before.
- [hard] REQ-05: Harness tests over archive planning own the derived-document property.

planning.outcome: Archiving an issue moves the files under its artifact directories along with its linked documents.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One extra root source in archive planning, consumed by the existing move execution.

title: Remove redundant explicit links inside artifact directories
description:
This repository's issue records drop explicit document links that add nothing once documents under an issue's artifact directory are derived: links to paths inside the owner's own directory that carry no type or label.

## Background

An issue's derived documents are the files under its resolved artifact directory in each declared documentation area. A derived document carries no type and no label, so an explicit link remains the way to attach that metadata, and the way to attach a path outside the directory.

A count over this repository found 11 of 542 explicit links pointing inside the owner's own canonical directory: 10 bare directory links and one file. Whether those links carry a type or label was not checked, so the set to remove may be smaller. One further link points inside another issue's directory and stays, as do the 530 links to paths outside any owner directory.

This is a one-time edit of repository data.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: No issue record holds an explicit document link without type and label whose path lies inside that issue's own artifact directory.
- [hard] REQ-02: Links carrying a type or label, and links to paths outside the owner's directory, are unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: The target of each removed link remains listed among the issue's documents as a derived document.
- [hard] REQ-04: Repository validation passes after the edit.

planning.outcome: This repository's records carry no metadata-free explicit link to a file inside the owning issue's artifact directory.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: A bounded data edit of at most eleven links across a few issue records.

footprint.uncertainty: Issue records under .jit/issues/ chosen by a link scan at execution time; the investigation counts 11 candidates with metadata unchecked.

title: Show word status markers in documented command output
description:
Documentation examples of command output show the word status markers the CLI prints, with no emoji or pictographic marker.

## Background

Human-readable CLI status output uses words (`error`, `warning`, `ok`) in place of emoji and pictographic markers. Several pages still quote the old output (line numbers at the investigation baseline):

- `docs/how-to/dependency-management.md:134-141,216-220,420-426`
- `docs/reference/worktree-validate.md:378-390`
- `docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md:139,313,344`
- `docs/reference/claim.md:363`
- `docs/tutorials/parallel-work-worktrees.md:127`
- `docs/concepts/core-model.md:638-645`, which shows output the code never prints
- `docs/concepts/design-philosophy.md:344-346`
- `docs/concepts/guarantees.md:541`
- `docs/how-to/custom-gates.md:53`
- `dev/authoring-conventions.md:323,342,364`

Prose do/don't lists are not output examples, and the type-icon example configuration stays.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each output example on these pages matches the text the command prints, with word status markers.
- [hard] REQ-02: No output example in the documentation contains an emoji or pictographic status marker.
- [hard] REQ-03: Type-icon examples are unchanged.

planning.outcome: Documented command output shows word status markers in place of emoji.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One known list of output examples on ten pages, edited against settled output.

title: Remove the record-reading profile subcommands
description:
The `profile list`, `profile validate`, `profile reconfigure` and `profile upgrade` subcommands are removed, because each exists to read or reconcile applied-profile records that charter decision D-8 deletes.

## Background

Profile packages apply once, and from then on the repository owns every value (`@/charter/D-8`). The ownership lifecycle that D-8 rejects surfaces as four subcommands:

- `profile list` and `profile validate` read applied-profile records and render their agreement with the installed package (`list_recorded_profiles` and `validate_recorded_profiles` at `crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:614,654`; `render_profile_agreement` at `crates/jit/src/main.rs:1192-1250`).
- `profile reconfigure` and `profile upgrade` re-derive a selection from the records (`profile.rs:1427-1621`, through `lifecycle_selection_from_sources` at `:1540`).

Their surfaces are:

- CLI variants (`crates/jit/src/cli.rs:2966-3330`) and dispatch arms (`main.rs:2623-2981`).
- Command-schema arms (`crates/jit/src/schema.rs:478-530`).
- MCP curated entries (`mcp-server/curated-tools.json:56-63`) and their tests.
- The failure-lever registry arms for these subcommands (`crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/failure_lever_registry.toml`, within 674-762), which the failure-probe coverage test checks against the command surface (`crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/failure_probe_coverage_tests.rs:258`).
- The release workflow's `profile list --json` smoke step (`.github/workflows/release-artifacts.yml:269`, asserted at `:280-294`).

Line numbers are at the investigation baseline. The records themselves and the lifecycle vocabulary are removed separately.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The `profile list`, `profile validate`, `profile reconfigure` and `profile upgrade` subcommands no longer parse, and the published command schema has no entry for them.
- [hard] REQ-02: Their executor functions, dispatch arms, renderers and the record-driven lifecycle selection are gone from the source.
- [hard] REQ-03: The MCP curated tool list names none of them, and the MCP tests pass.
- [hard] REQ-04: The failure-lever registry holds no arm for a removed subcommand, and the failure-probe coverage test passes.
- [hard] REQ-05: No release workflow step invokes a removed subcommand.
- [hard] REQ-06: Tests that exercised only the removed subcommands are deleted, and no surviving test invokes them.

planning.outcome: No profile subcommand reads applied-profile records or reconciles a repository with an installed package.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: A mechanical removal of four subcommands along one command surface, with no behaviour added.

title: Produce the shipped workflow package by packing its directory
description:
The release workflow and the package-content documentation check produce the shipped workflow package by packing its source directory, so neither depends on profile capture.

## Background

Package authors edit a package manifest directly (`@/charter/D-8`), and pack turns a package directory into an archive. Two scripts still produce the package through capture, which rewrites a package from the repository:

- The release workflow builds the release package with capture (`.github/workflows/release-artifacts.yml:122-140`).
- The package-content documentation check runs capture and then shows the result (`scripts/docs-check-package-content.sh:141-151`). It is wired into the mechanical documentation checks (`scripts/docs-mechanical.sh:103`), and its self-test exercises that path (`scripts/docs-check-selftest.sh:43,84,100,420`).

Line numbers are at the investigation baseline. Capture still exists while these scripts move; it is removed afterwards.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The release workflow produces its package archive by packing the package directory, and no workflow step invokes capture.
- [hard] REQ-02: The package-content documentation check verifies package content through pack without invoking capture.
- [hard] REQ-03: The documentation-check self-test passes over the changed check.

planning.outcome: The release workflow and the package-content check produce the package with pack instead of capture.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Two scripts and one workflow step switched to an existing subcommand, with no Rust change.

title: Remove profile capture
description:
`profile capture` and its contribution reconciliation are removed: package authors edit the manifest directly, and pack produces an archive from the package directory.

## Background

Charter decision D-8 deletes capture's reconciliation: the repository owns its values, and a package author edits the package manifest. Capture (`crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:744-854`) rewrites a package from the repository through the reconciliation in `crates/jit/src/profile/package_capture.rs` (`refresh_contributions` 439, `published_identities` 505, `read_registry` 558, `republished_manifest` 594, `write_contribution_values` 667, the `CapturedContribution*` types 101-130). That path rewrites a contribution as a single-line inline table and leaves package identity out of step, both reported by a downstream lead. No script or workflow invokes capture any longer.

The package tree reader (`capture_package_tree`) serves pack and add and stays.

Capture's surfaces are its CLI variant (`crates/jit/src/cli.rs`), dispatch arm (`crates/jit/src/main.rs`), command-schema arm (`crates/jit/src/schema.rs`), MCP curated entry (`mcp-server/curated-tools.json`), and a failure-lever arm (`crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/failure_lever_registry.toml`, within 674-762) that the failure-probe coverage test checks against the command surface. Line numbers are at the investigation baseline.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The `profile capture` subcommand no longer parses and has no command-schema or MCP curated entry.
- [hard] REQ-02: Capture's contribution reconciliation is gone from the package-capture module, and the package tree reader used by pack and add remains.
- [hard] REQ-03: The failure-lever registry holds no capture arm, and the failure-probe coverage test passes.
- [hard] REQ-04: Capture tests are deleted, and pack and add tests pass unchanged.

planning.outcome: No capture path exists; package authors edit the manifest and pack produces the archive.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One subcommand and its reconciliation helpers, removed after its last script caller moved.

title: Remove the profile selector tags
description:
A profile selector is a bare package directory path: the `id:` and `path:` selector tags, the `profile show` id argument and its `applied` field are removed.

## Background

A `--profile` selector today carries a tag (`ProfileSelector`, `crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:120`): `id:NAME` resolves a package only through the applied record (`profile.rs:546-559`), and `path:DIR` reads a package directory. Charter decision D-8 deletes the records, so `id:` has no resolution route left. Redefining `id:` over a declared packages root was considered and rejected: it adds mechanism where a path already names the package (`@/charter/D-18`). With `id:` gone, `path:` is a prefix with one alternative, so it goes too and a selector is the directory path itself. `profile show` takes an id argument and prints an `applied` field (`ProfileShowEntry.applied` in `crates/jit/src/profile/application.rs`).

Callers select with tags in several places:

- Three skills (`.agents/skills/jit-manage/SKILL.md:82`, `.agents/skills/jit-migrate/SKILL.md:26`, `.agents/skills/jit-project-lead/SKILL.md:200`).
- The release workflow's dry run (`.github/workflows/release-artifacts.yml:270`).
- Failure-lever arms (`crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/failure_lever_registry.toml:696,705,714,887`), checked by the failure-probe coverage test.
- The acceptance tests and MCP integration tests (`crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/profile_acceptance_tests.rs:288`, `mcp-server/test-integration.js`).

Line numbers are at the investigation baseline. The selector type keeps one variant here; unwrapping it into the path it holds is separate work.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A selector is read as a package directory path; an argument beginning `id:` or `path:` is refused with an error that names the bare-path form.
- [hard] REQ-02: The selector's id variant and its resolution through applied records are gone from the source.
- [hard] REQ-03: `profile show` accepts a package path only, and its output has no `applied` field.
- [hard] REQ-04: The skills, the release workflow, the failure-lever arms and the MCP integration tests select packages by bare path, and the failure-probe coverage and MCP tests pass.

planning.outcome: A profile selector is a bare package directory path; the show id argument and the applied field are gone.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One selector grammar and one show argument with their bounded set of callers outside the crate.

title: Remove profile checks from repository validation
description:
Repository validation stops checking profile ownership and stops repairing profile provenance, because charter decision D-8 deletes profile validation and its checks inside repository validation.

## Background

After D-8 an edit to a value a package contributed is an ordinary repository change, and git shows and restores it. Repository validation still carries the ownership machinery:

- The `profile-ownership` rule (`collect_profile_ownership_findings` and `PROFILE_OWNERSHIP_RULE`, `crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:639-700`) reports divergence from an applied record. It produced the downstream report where editing a contributed gate field failed validation and the suggested remedy made the state worse.
- Validation repair performs profile provenance repair from the record (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:650-1030`, with `with_profile_ownership_findings` at 745, record readers at 835-970, and the record list at 406).

Tests: `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/derived_state_repair_tests.rs` (216, 365, 445-825) and `crates/jit/tests/cli_item_validate/derived_state_repair_tests.rs` (110, 226, 327, 378); `.config/nextest.toml:22` names tests in the validate command module that go. Another stream edits `validate.rs:1835-2640`, a disjoint region. Line numbers are at the investigation baseline.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Repository validation reports no `profile-ownership` rule and reads no applied-profile record or package.
- [hard] REQ-02: Validation repair performs no profile provenance repair.
- [hard] REQ-03: The removed rule's tests and the profile repair tests are deleted, and the test-runner configuration names no deleted test.
- [hard] REQ-04: Validating a repository that never applied a profile yields the same findings as before.

planning.outcome: Repository validation emits no profile-ownership finding, and its repair mode reads no package.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One rule and one repair branch in two validation modules, both removals.

title: Remove three-way profile publication
description:
Profile composition decides each target from the packages being applied alone: three-way publication, base fingerprints, record claims in composition, conflict remedies and the diverged conflict class are removed.

## Background

Charter decision D-8 rejects three-way publication and conflict remedies. Today composition compares a candidate package with the applied record and the repository:

- The three-way decision lives in `crates/jit/src/profile/three_way.rs`.
- Base fingerprints are at `crates/jit/src/repository_state/profile_apply.rs:1069-1365`.
- Record-ownership composition is at `profile_apply.rs:2197-2256,2466-2760`, with `claimed_target_state` at 2760-2877 and `contribution_disposition` at 2401-2459. Its holding branch makes an upgrade refuse with one package named twice.
- Remedies are `ProfileRemedy`/`ProfileResolution` (733-806) and `remedy_suggestions` (993), with the diverged class beside them.
- Asset retention and departure are at 1990-2196.
- Repair claims are built in `crates/jit/src/profile/apply_claims.rs`, and owner, retain and remove vocabulary sits in `crates/jit/src/profile/difference.rs`.

The conflict error-code description links a remedy contract (`crates/jit/src/output.rs:966-970`); the generated error-code reference (`docs/reference/error-codes.md`) is rendered from it. Error suggestions name deleted commands and records (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:1263,1280-1283`). The diff command's help names recorded claims (`crates/jit/src/cli.rs:3016-3041`). Line numbers are at the investigation baseline.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The three-way decision module, base fingerprints and record-claim composition are gone, and composition reads no applied-profile record.
- [hard] REQ-02: A profile conflict arises only between packages being applied that define one key differently; the repository's current value is never a conflict party.
- [hard] REQ-03: No conflict carries a remedy, and the diverged class is gone from conflict output and its schema.
- [hard] REQ-04: Error suggestions, help text and the conflict error-code description name no removed command, record or remedy, and the generated error-code reference is regenerated from that description.
- [hard] REQ-05: Composition unit tests cover the surviving conflict rule, and tests of three-way and remedy behaviour are deleted.

planning.outcome: Composition decides a target from package contents alone; fingerprints, record claims and remedies are gone.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: A removal confined to the composition module and its two helper modules, with one surviving conflict rule.

title: Remove applied-profile records
description:
Profile application and selection neither write nor read applied-profile records: the record type, its writes under the data root, its layout constant, record conflicts and record-driven dependency resolution are removed.

## Background

Charter decision D-8 deletes applied-profile records. No released record format exists, so a repository holding records drops them with no migration (`@/inv/canonical-cutover`). Record code remains in several modules (line numbers at the investigation baseline):

- `crates/jit/src/repository_state/profile_apply.rs`: `AppliedProfileRecord` (1395) and record handling (1057-1510).
- `crates/jit/src/repository_state/initialize.rs`: profiles directory creation (1057-1063), `InstalledRecordConflict` (152), `profile_record_changed` (637) and `serialize_profile_record` (1141).
- The data-root layout constant `VirtualPath::PROFILES` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/path.rs:305`).
- `crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs`: the record readers (`applied_record_path` 2466, `read_applied_profile_record` 2191, `read_applied_record` 2986, 2377-2600, 2631-2812), and the applied-package graph candidates (`resolve_applied_profile_packages` 1679, `resolve_profile_graph_with_applied` 1640, the record fallback in `resolve_dependency_package_from` 1757-1790).
- `crates/jit/src/profile/variables.rs`: record-based resolution (`resolve_package_from_record` 324 and its helpers).
- `crates/jit/src/profile/agreement.rs`: the agreement report over records.

The lifecycle event's status is classified today by whether a record existed (`profile_lifecycle_profile`, `initialize.rs:1081`). Here that classification stops reading a record and is computed from what the apply publishes; redefining the status vocabulary is separate work.

Failure-injection fixtures name a malformed record (`crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/failure_lever_registry.toml:674-762`, `crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/failure_probe_fixture.rs`). A cutover test holds a record-authority guard (`crates/jit/tests/scratch_build/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs`) that another stream also edits.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: No code path reads or writes applied-profile records, and the data-root layout declares no profiles directory.
- [hard] REQ-02: A dependency resolves only from the selection's own package closure; previously applied packages are no longer candidates.
- [hard] REQ-03: The lifecycle event's status is computed without reading a record, and re-applying identical content reports no change.
- [hard] REQ-04: Failure-injection fixtures and tests name no record, and the failure-probe coverage test passes.

planning.outcome: Profile application and selection neither write nor read applied-profile records.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The last consumers of one record type, removed together so the build stays green.

title: Record what was applied in the profile lifecycle event
description:
The profile lifecycle event records what an apply did: the package id, its version and the variable values applied, with a status vocabulary that no longer refers to records, reconfigure or upgrade.

## Background

Charter decision D-8: "The profile operation's event records what was applied." The lifecycle vocabulary (`crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs:1143-1166`) carries reconfigure and upgrade operations and statuses, and its installed status is defined as "no prior record existed". The event payload (`ProfileLifecycleProfile`, `types.rs:1181`) holds id, status and variables but no version. Line numbers are at the investigation baseline.

Struct literals of the event are built in `crates/jit/src/domain/event_log.rs:101`, `crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs:2522` and `crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store_tests.rs:2360`, and the event is assembled in `crates/jit/src/repository_state/initialize.rs` (`profile_lifecycle_profile`). The event catalog (`crates/jit/src/domain/event_catalog.rs:264`) describes the payload as "without resolved values"; the generated events reference (`docs/reference/events.md`) is rendered from that catalog.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The lifecycle operation and status vocabularies hold no reconfigure or upgrade member, and no status is defined by a record's presence.
- [hard] REQ-02: The profile lifecycle event records the package id, its version and the variable values applied.
- [hard] REQ-03: The event catalog describes that payload, and the generated events reference is regenerated from it.
- [hard] REQ-04: Unit tests over event construction own the payload properties.

planning.outcome: The lifecycle event names the package id, version and variables applied, with a record-free status vocabulary.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One event payload and its two vocabularies, with a handful of literal construction sites.

title: Write the package value over an existing registry entry
description:
Applying a package writes the package's value over the entry a registry holds under the same identity, so a newer package version or new variable values take effect and the adopter keeps local edits through git.

## Background

Charter decision D-8 says applying "writes the new rendering". The registry renderers are insert-only today: each returns early when an entry under the contributed identity exists, whatever that entry says (`merge_scalar`, `merge_map_entry`, `merge_set_string`, `merge_keyed_array`, `merge_projection` at `crates/jit/src/repository_state/profile_apply.rs:3101-3276`, contract described at 2370-2399; line numbers at the investigation baseline).

The chosen semantics is whole-entry replacement under the identity. A deep merge was rejected: it keeps fields the package no longer declares and adds a merge engine that git already provides. Keeping insert-only was rejected because it contradicts D-8.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: For each contribution kind, applying a package whose value differs from the entry the registry holds under the same identity leaves the package's value in the registry.
- [hard] REQ-02: Replacement is whole-entry: no field of the prior entry survives unless the package value declares it.
- [hard] REQ-03: Entries under identities the package does not contribute keep their bytes.
- [hard] REQ-04: Unit tests over the registry renderers own replacement semantics for each contribution kind.

planning.outcome: Applying a package replaces an existing registry entry under the same identity with the package's value.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One behavioural change applied uniformly to the five renderers in one module.

title: Let the dependent package win a key both packages declare
description:
Profile composition resolves a key that two packages declare by their declared dependency order, with the dependent package winning, and refuses two unrelated packages that declare one key differently.

## Background

Charter decision D-8 composes packages "in declared dependency order with the dependent package winning a key both declare" and "refuses two unrelated packages that declare one key differently". Today `compose_contribution_identity` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/profile_apply.rs:350-383` at the investigation baseline) contests every differing definition, so a workflow package cannot override a value its base package contributes. The order derives from dependencies the manifests declare, so the rule is mechanism over declared data (`@/inv/domain-agnostic`). Composition receives that order from the profile selection the command layer builds once per invocation (`crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs`), which holds the resolved package graph.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: When one package depends on another, directly or transitively, and both define one key, the dependent package's value is composed.
- [hard] REQ-02: When two packages with no dependency path between them define one key differently, composition refuses with a conflict naming both packages.
- [hard] REQ-03: Two packages defining one key identically compose without conflict.
- [hard] REQ-04: A property test shows the composed result is independent of the order in which packages are selected.

planning.outcome: Composition resolves a key two packages declare by dependency order and refuses unrelated packages that differ.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One composition rule in one function, fed the dependency order the selection already holds.

title: Build one profile selection per invocation
description:
Plan, apply, diff and repository initialization reach package selection through one selection value built once per invocation, which resolves selectors, the package graph and variable inputs once.

## Background

Selection preparation is repeated across the profile executor (`crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs`, line numbers at the investigation baseline):

- Separate skeletons exist in `plan_profiles_with_inputs` (1168), `plan_profiles_from_sources` (1201), `apply_profile_with_inputs` (1285), `apply_profile_from_sources` (1342), `diff_profiles_from_sources` (1388) and `apply_profile_package_with_inputs` (1818).
- Each `*_from_sources` entry resolves selectors and the graph, then its `*_with_inputs` routine resolves both again (1206/1173, 1347/1290).
- Initialization resolves three times: `crates/jit/src/commands/init.rs:133-137,166-167` plus a preflight through `validate_profile_selection` (1792) from `crates/jit/src/main.rs:2552`.
- `prepare_profile_selection` (2040) captures the repository three times and rebuilds its inputs three times (`profile_selection_inputs`, 2943), composing each package at least 2 + 4N times.
- Variable inputs are validated at load (500) and again at 1177, 1293, 1403, 1824 and `init.rs:169`.
- Package model references are validated in the package constructor (`crates/jit/src/profile/package.rs:623`) and again in `resolve_package` (`crates/jit/src/profile/variables.rs:311`).

The pure graph resolution (`ResolvedProfileGraph::resolve`, `crates/jit/src/profile/graph.rs:50`) stays the domain function. One command-layer selection, built from the selectors and variable options, holds the selected packages, their closure, the resolved graph, the validated inputs and the resolved content. The preparation step takes that value in place of four parallel slices with a length check (2050). Initialization's preflight becomes building the selection before its session opens.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Plan, apply, diff and initialization with a profile each resolve selectors and the package dependency graph once per invocation.
- [hard] REQ-02: Composition inputs are built once per invocation.
- [hard] REQ-03: Variable-input validation and package model reference validation each run once per command.
- [hard] REQ-04: Initialization reaches selection through the same path as apply, with no separate preflight resolution.
- [hard] REQ-05: A counting probe at the harness layer observes the once-per-invocation properties.

planning.outcome: Plan, apply, diff and init resolve selectors, the package graph and variable inputs once through one selection value.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One value replacing a repeated preparation skeleton inside one executor module and its init caller.

title: Refuse a profile apply over uncommitted target changes
description:
In a git repository, applying a profile refuses while a path it would write differs from the committed tree, so writing the new rendering never discards an uncommitted local edit; without git it proceeds.

## Background

Charter decision D-8: applying a newer version or other variable values "refuses while the files it writes carry uncommitted changes, then writes the new rendering, and the adopter keeps local edits through git". Core commands work without git (`@/charter/D-4`); there the diff command is the comparison to read before applying, so apply proceeds. Initialization over an absent data root has nothing to protect.

No production code detects uncommitted files today. The test-only `GitRevisionResolver::changed_worktree_paths` is being deleted elsewhere and stays deleted. Git access goes through one storage-owned module that runs the git CLI (`@/charter/D-21`), so the dirty-path query is an operation of that module.

The refusal is a read check before the mutation session opens. The redo record's preimage comparison remains the concurrency guard.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: In a git repository, apply refuses before publishing when a path it would write differs from HEAD (modified, staged, or untracked).
- [hard] REQ-02: The refusal is self-explanatory: its message and JSON details name each uncommitted path and state that committing or discarding those changes lets the apply proceed.
- [hard] REQ-03: Apply proceeds when its target paths are clean, even while unrelated paths are dirty.
- [hard] REQ-04: Without git, apply proceeds.
- [hard] REQ-05: Initialization with an absent data root is never refused.
- [hard] REQ-06: The dirty-path query is an operation of the storage-owned git module and has no other implementation.

planning.outcome: In a git repository apply refuses while a path it writes differs from HEAD; without git it proceeds.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One read check before the session plus one query on an existing git module.

footprint.uncertainty: The git query lands in the storage-owned git CLI module another epic introduces; its file path is fixed when that module exists.

title: Prune dead and test-only profile executor entry points
description:
The profile executor and repository initialization expose only entry points that production dispatch reaches; tests drive those entries.

## Background

Executor entry points by production reachability (`crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs`, `crates/jit/src/commands/init.rs`, line numbers at the investigation baseline):

- Dead: `plan_profile` (1221) with its chain, and `initialize_profiled_repository_from_sources` (`init.rs:89`).
- Test-only: `plan_profiles` (1163), `apply_profile` (1274), `apply_profile_package` (1807) with `apply_profile_package_with_inputs` (1818) and `resolve_profile_closure` (1622), `initialize_profiled_repository` (`init.rs:79`), and the test-gated `prepare_profile` (1995).
- Production: `initialize_fresh_repository` (`init.rs:105`) is called by the server (`crates/server/src/routes.rs:1115`) and stays.

About 76 unit tests and `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/derived_state_repair_tests.rs` drive `apply_profile_package`. Many re-prove composition properties that the composition module's own tests own; for example, order independence is tested at `profile.rs:5697` and at `crates/jit/src/repository_state/profile_apply.rs:4085`. Each property has one owning test (`@/inv/orthogonal-tests`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: No public profile executor or initialization entry point lacks a production caller.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each test that drove a pruned entry point drives the surviving one, or is deleted when it re-proves a property the composition module's tests own.
- [hard] REQ-03: Fresh-repository initialization through the server keeps working.

planning.outcome: The profile executor exposes only the entry points production dispatch reaches.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: A removal of a known list of entry points with a test migration onto one surviving entry.

title: Report profile plans through the apply result type
description:
A profile dry run is a read-only run of the apply computation, including final validation, and returns the apply result type; the twin plan types, the twin status enums and the trait bridging them are removed.

## Background

Plan and apply report through parallel types in `crates/jit/src/profile/application.rs` (line numbers at the investigation baseline):

- Result types: `ProfileApplyResult` (41) and `ProfilePlanEntry` (272).
- Status enums: `ProfileApplicationStatus` (11) and `ProfilePlanStatus` (256).
- The bridging trait `SelectionObservation` (80, implementations at 93 and 105).

The apply command's output schema is a hand-written `oneOf` over both (`crates/jit/src/schema.rs:514-530`). Both routes call the same preparation, but only apply runs final validation (`crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:1891-1900`), so a dry run can succeed where the apply fails.

A preview runs the same mutation session as its operation, read-only (`@/charter/D-20`). One run over the profile selection takes a mode: publish, rehearse, or report. The existing refuse-or-report conflict response (`profile.rs:104`) already switches between apply and diff.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Plan and apply return one result type with one status enum; the twin types and the bridging trait are gone.
- [hard] REQ-02: A dry run fails exactly where the apply would, including on final validation findings, and publishes nothing.
- [hard] REQ-03: The apply command's published output schema is derived from the result type, and the hand-written alternative schema is gone.
- [hard] REQ-04: Human-readable plan and apply output both render from the one result type.
- [hard] REQ-05: The MCP integration tests pass over the unified apply output.

planning.outcome: A dry run executes the apply computation read-only, including final validation, and returns the apply result.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One result type replacing a pair, with its schema derived and one mode switch on the run.

title: Derive profile conflict serialization
description:
Profile conflict and target-subject types serialize through derived implementations, and profile conflict error details publish a derived schema; the hand-written wire mirrors are removed.

## Background

In `crates/jit/src/repository_state/profile_apply.rs` (line numbers at the investigation baseline):

- `ProfileTargetConflictWire` (810) and the hand-written `Serialize` for `ProfileTargetConflict` (827) exist to inject a computed `remedy` field, which no longer exists.
- `ProfileTargetSubjectWire` (911) and the hand-written `Serialize` for `ProfileTargetSubject` (916) exist to render a virtual path through `repository_relative()`; a field-level serializer or a path newtype derives the same output.
- `ProfileTargetConflictsError` (969) and `ProfileTargetConflictEntry` (936) derive `Serialize` but not `JsonSchema`, and reach JSON as error details (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:1290`) with no published schema.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: No hand-written `Serialize` or `JsonSchema` implementation, and no wire mirror type, remains for profile conflict or target-subject types.
- [hard] REQ-02: Profile conflict error details have a published schema derived from their type.
- [hard] REQ-03: A target subject serializes as its repository-relative path.

planning.outcome: Profile conflict and target-subject types serialize through derived impls with a published error-detail schema.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Three serialization impls replaced by derives in one module, plus one schema registration.

title: Name profile conflict parties by package only
description:
One conflict-origin type names the parties of a profile conflict, and it holds package identities only, because after charter decision D-8 the repository is never a conflict party.

## Background

`ContributionConflictOwner` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/profile_apply.rs:241`) and `ProfileConflictOccupant` (`:586`) are one enum, `{Repository, Package(id)}`, with two wire spellings: one derives `Serialize` with default PascalCase tags and no schema, the other uses kebab-case with a schema (line numbers at the investigation baseline). Composition now conflicts only between packages being applied, so the repository variant has no producer.

- [hard] REQ-01: One type names a conflict's parties, and it holds package identities only.
- [hard] REQ-02: The repository variant and the second enum are gone.
- [hard] REQ-03: Conflict output and its derived schema spell parties one way.

planning.outcome: One conflict-origin type names the packages in a conflict, in one wire spelling.

title: Fold the profile dependency error into the graph error
description:
Each package-graph refusal surfaces as the one graph error type and maps to the profile error code; the command-layer mirror and its field-by-field translator are removed.

## Background

`ProfileDependencyError` (`crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:262`) mirrors `ProfileGraphError` (`crates/jit/src/profile/graph.rs:215`) through the translator `profile_graph_error` (`profile.rs:2317`). Its fallback arm (`:2372`) sends `SelectedPackageMissing`, `MissingDependency` and four invalid-version variants to the generic error code, because only the mirror is downcast to the profile code (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:144,1276`). The graph error is pure and stays in the graph module. A dependency loading failure that needs I/O context is at most one command-layer variant, which keeps dependencies pointing inward (`@/inv/architecture-dependency-direction`).

- [hard] REQ-02: Each graph error variant maps to the profile error code and exit status, shown by a test over the variants.
- [hard] REQ-03: A dependency loading failure needing I/O context is at most one command-layer error variant.

title: Use one validated profile package type
description:
Apply, pack and add read a profile package through one validated in-memory type; the parallel captured-tree type folds into it.

## Background

`ProfilePackage` and `CapturedPackageTree` (`crates/jit/src/profile/package_capture.rs:133`) are parallel validated-package types. Both are built through `ProfilePackage::validate_content` (`compose_captured_tree`, `package_capture.rs:697`). The captured tree serves pack (`pack_profile_package_inner`, `crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:883`) and add (`read_package_archive`, `crates/jit/src/profile/package_archive.rs:391`), while apply reads `ProfilePackage::from_directory`. The captured tree carries the package files that pack and add need, so the merged type keeps them. Test helpers build captured trees (`crates/jit/src/test_utils.rs`). - [hard] REQ-02: A package read for apply, read for pack, and extracted by add has the same identity hash on each route.
- [hard] REQ-03: Pack and add tests pass over the merged type.

title: Unwrap the single-variant package source enum
description:
`ProfilePackageSource` is replaced by the directory path it wraps, because its only variant is `Directory`.

## Background

`ProfilePackageSource` (`crates/jit/src/profile/package.rs:45`) has one variant, `Directory(PathBuf)`, destructured irrefutably at `crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:1762,2310`. - [hard] REQ-02: Package loading behaves as before for each caller, shown by the existing package tests.

title: Make the profile selector a package path

`ProfileSelector` is replaced by the package directory path it holds, because a selector carries no tag.

A `--profile` selector is a bare package directory path, with no `id:` or `path:` tag (`@/charter/D-18`). `ProfileSelector` (`crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:120`) is left with one variant holding that path. title: Serialize a profile origin as its directory path
description:
`ProfileOrigin` is replaced by the worktree-relative directory path it wraps, and a package origin serializes as that path in results, events and schemas.

`ProfileOrigin` (`crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs:1130`) has one variant, `Directory(RootRelativePath)`, and serializes as a tagged object (`{"source": "directory", "location": ...}`). title: Derive registry target paths from one registry declaration
description:
Registry target paths derive from one registry declaration built on the data-root path constants, each registry renderer finds an existing entry through the one presence lookup, and each registry document is parsed once per composition.

## Background

In `crates/jit/src/repository_state/profile_apply.rs` (line numbers at the investigation baseline):

- Registry target paths are spelled four times: `Contribution::registry_path` (65-72), `ContributionRegistry::path` (149-157), `KeyedArrayTarget::registry_path` (513-520), and the match in `Contribution::semantic_identity` (106-115).

- `contribution_in_registry` (2912) owns the presence lookup, but the scalar, map-entry, set, keyed-array and projection renderers each test presence their own way (3101-3276).
- `render_composed_contribution` (3066) re-parses the registry through `semantic_document` (3278) per contribution, and `contribution_in_registry` re-parses per identity.

`ContributionRegistry` becomes the one declaration, with its path derived from the path constants. A keyed-array target and a contribution return their registry, and initialization reuses the same constants.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each registry's target path is spelled once, in the registry declaration built on the data-root path constants.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each registry renderer finds an existing entry through the one presence lookup.
- [hard] REQ-03: A composition parses each registry document once, however many contributions it renders, shown by a parse-count probe.
- [hard] REQ-04: Composition unit tests own these properties.

planning.outcome: Registry paths come from one declaration, renderers share one presence lookup, and each registry is parsed once per composition.

title: Show a package's target set without value hashes
description:
`profile show` prints the paths a package targets without per-target hash values, and per-target value hashing is removed; the package identity hash stays.

## Background

`ProfilePackageHashes::targets` (`crates/jit/src/profile/package.rs:910-971`) computes a hash per target. Its keys give the target set (`crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs:2052`), and its values are printed by `profile show` (`crates/jit/src/profile/application.rs:149`), their only consumer. - [hard] REQ-02: Per-target value hashing is gone from the package and variable-resolution modules, together with the private canonical-JSON helpers that served only that hashing.

- [hard] REQ-04: The package identity hash of each shipped package is unchanged.

title: Keep one canonical JSON function
description:
The core crate has one canonical-JSON function, in repository-state serialization, and a unit test fails when `serde_json`'s `preserve_order` feature is enabled.

## Background

At the investigation baseline five private canonical-JSON copies existed. Three serve only mechanisms that earlier work removes: the profile composition copy served record fingerprints, and the copies in `crates/jit/src/profile/package.rs` (near line 980) and `crates/jit/src/profile/variables.rs` (near 512) served per-target value hashing. The manifest v1 decoder's `canonicalize` in `crates/jit/src/profile/wire.rs` is removed by the manifest v2 cutover. The survivor is in `crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs` (`canonical_json` and `canonicalize_json`, 576-588), which serializes issues, gate runs, events and presets. This work converges whatever copies remain when it lands, including any that profile package identity hashing still reaches.

`serde_json`'s `preserve_order` feature is off in this workspace, so `serde_json::Map` is a sorted map and each recursive canonicalize helper is an identity transform. The order-bearing step is `serde_json::to_value`, which turns struct field order into sorted key order; the on-disk record format pins that sorted output. The survivor therefore keeps `to_value` followed by serialization. `serde_json` exposes no configuration flag for the feature, so a unit test is the guard: it serializes a struct whose fields are declared out of key order and asserts sorted bytes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Exactly one canonical-JSON function exists in the core crate, in repository-state serialization, and each former copy's callers use it.
- [hard] REQ-02: Bytes written for issues, gate runs, events and presets are unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: A unit test fails when `serde_json`'s `preserve_order` feature is enabled.
- [hard] REQ-04: The package identity hash of each shipped package is unchanged.

planning.outcome: One canonical-JSON function serializes sorted-key bytes for its callers, and a test fails when key order is preserved.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One surviving function and a handful of private copies redirected to it.

title: Type profile versions as semver values
description:
Profile package versions and version requirements are semver types in the package model, parsed once at decode, and graph resolution has no error variant for an unparseable version.

## Background

Versions are strings in the model (`crates/jit/src/profile/manifest.rs:136,139,168,176` at the investigation baseline). They are parsed and discarded in `validate_manifest_declarations` (`crates/jit/src/profile/package.rs:634-660`), then re-parsed in `ResolvedProfileGraph::resolve` (`crates/jit/src/profile/graph.rs:65,72,98,105,137,145`). That re-parse keeps four unreachable error variants: `InvalidPackageVersion` (220), `InvalidEngineRequirement` (227), `InvalidDependencyRequirement` (247) and `InvalidIncompatibilityRequirement` (266). The application input (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/profile_apply.rs:1513-1517`), the result types (`crates/jit/src/profile/application.rs`) and the version the profile lifecycle event records (`crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs`) carry versions as strings. Manifest decoding is in `crates/jit/src/profile/wire.rs`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Package version is `semver::Version` and each version requirement (engine compatibility, dependency, incompatibility) is `semver::VersionReq` in the package model, and the lifecycle event's version is `semver::Version`.
- [hard] REQ-02: A malformed version or requirement is rejected at manifest decode.
- [hard] REQ-03: Graph resolution has no error variant for an unparseable version or requirement.
- [hard] REQ-04: Serialized manifests, results and published schemas render versions as the same strings as before.

## Notes

- `semver` is a direct dependency with only its default features (`crates/jit/Cargo.toml:54`). The model derives `Serialize` and `JsonSchema` (`manifest.rs:130`), so `semver` needs `features = ["serde"]`. schemars 0.8.22's `semver` feature implements `JsonSchema` for `Version` only, not `VersionReq`, so both fields take `#[schemars(with = "String")]` and no schemars feature is enabled.
- `VersionReq` has no `Ord`, so the sort at `graph.rs:127` needs an explicit key.

planning.outcome: Package versions and requirements are parsed once at decode into semver types; graph resolution has no version-parse error.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One field type change through the model, its decoder, and the graph resolver.

title: Rewrite the profiles reference around apply-once
description:
The adopter reference pages and contributor notes describe profiles as packages that apply once, with no applied-profile records, ownership, remedies or capture.

## Background

Charter decision D-8 replaces the ownership lifecycle with apply-once. Applying composes packages in dependency order with the dependent package winning a key both declare, refuses unrelated packages that declare one key differently, and writes the package value over an existing entry. A selector is a bare package directory path. The diff command shows where a repository differs from a package. The profile lifecycle event records the package id, version and variables applied. The refusal to apply over uncommitted target changes is documented with that behaviour, separately.

Pages describing the removed lifecycle (line numbers at the investigation baseline):

- `docs/reference/profiles.md`: intro 7-10, the record 24-26, list/show/validate/capture and `id:` 223-277, conflicts 328-397, the remedy contract 398-450, provenance repair 491-514, publication and records 524-570.
- Other reference pages: `docs/reference/storage-format.md:27,87-89`, `docs/concepts/guarantees.md:160,661-662`, `docs/reference/worktree-validate.md:319-336,392-395`, `docs/index.md:53`. The events and error-code references are generated from code and follow it.
- Contributor material: `dev/index.md:112-138` (capturing the workflow package) and `dev/architecture/repository-state-materialization.md:197-214`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The profiles reference states apply-once semantics: replacement of existing entries, dependent-wins composition, refusal of unrelated conflicts, and bare-path selectors.
- [hard] REQ-02: No adopter page describes applied-profile records, ownership claims, fingerprints, remedies, capture, reconfigure, upgrade, list, profile validation or selector tags.
- [hard] REQ-03: The storage format, guarantees and worktree validation pages match the surviving behaviour.
- [hard] REQ-04: The contributor index describes producing the workflow package by packing its directory, and the materialization note carries no ownership text.

planning.outcome: Profile reference pages describe apply, diff, pack and add with no records, ownership or remedies.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One documentation family rewritten against one settled behaviour.

title: Describe the uncommitted-target refusal in the profile references
description:
The profiles reference and the profile apply command entry describe how applying a package refuses over uncommitted target changes in a git repository and proceeds without git.

## Background

Applying a newer package version or other variable values writes the new rendering over the repository's files, and the adopter keeps local edits through git (`@/charter/D-8`). In a git repository apply therefore refuses while a path it would write differs from HEAD, naming those paths. Without git it proceeds, and the diff command is the comparison to read before applying (`@/charter/D-4`). Initialization over an absent data root is never refused.

The pages are the apply section of `docs/reference/profiles.md` and the profile apply entry of `docs/reference/cli-commands.md`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The profiles reference states when apply refuses over uncommitted target changes, how to proceed, and that apply proceeds without git.
- [hard] REQ-02: The profile apply command entry describes the refusal and its JSON error.
- [hard] REQ-03: Both pages state that initialization over an absent data root is exempt.

planning.outcome: The profile references describe the uncommitted-target refusal and its no-git behaviour.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Two sections on two pages describing one settled refusal.
